claim_boundary: Finite-height normalization, logarithmic reduction, factorization, continuity, and the symmetric half-weight limit at y=1 are Lean-verified. The nonzero-frequency scalar Perron limit remains unproved; no RH progress or novel mathematics is claimed.
verified_units: positive vertical line avoids the pole at zero
complex power equals the exponential-logarithmic kernel for y > 0
finite-height y-form equals the a = log(y) oscillatory form
the constant exp(a*c) factors exactly from the finite-height integral
the scalar and logarithmic open targets are logically equivalent
all finite scalar truncations are interval integrable
at y = 1 the raw integral equals 2*arctan(T/c)
at y = 1 the normalized symmetric limit is 1/2

open_unit.statement_shape: For c > 0 and a != 0, the normalized symmetric integral of exp(i*a*t)/(c+i*t) has limit exp(-a*c) when a > 0 and zero when a < 0.
open_unit.why_open: The kernel decays only as 1/|t|, so the available absolute-integrability Fourier inversion theorem does not apply. A Dirichlet-type estimate, sharp truncation argument, or a proved comparison with a regularized inversion theorem is still required.
